title: Test crosses and unknown genotypes — video support
purpose: Use a homozygous recessive tester to distinguish possible parental genotypes and explain uncertainty from small samples.
fallback: One aa offspring from B_ × bb means the dominant-phenotype parent must carry the recessive allele, assuming the model, parentage and observations are correct. It is heterozygous. By contrast, several dominant offspring do not logically prove the parent is homozygous. An Aa parent can, by chance, produce a run of A-bearing gametes. For four independent offspring in an Aa × aa cross, the probability that all show the dominant phenotype is (1/2)⁴ = 1/16. More offspring with no recessive phenotype generally strengthen the homozygous interpretation, but finite samples still require cautious wording. Say what the evidence supports and what remains possible.

title: Single-trait crosses and probability — video support
purpose: Construct and interpret a monohybrid Punnett square, distinguish genotype and phenotype probabilities, and state the denominator.
fallback: For Aa × Aa, the four equally likely combinations are AA, Aa, aA and aa. Grouping the two heterozygous combinations gives probabilities of 1/4 AA, 1/2 Aa and 1/4 aa. The dominant phenotype has probability 3/4 under complete dominance. Genotype probability and phenotype probability therefore can differ. “Heterozygous” refers to two of the four combinations, while “dominant phenotype” includes three. Mark the requested group before choosing your numerator. When converting to an expected number, multiply by the total. If 80 offspring each have a 1/4 chance of aa, the expected number is 80 × 0.25 = 20. The result is an expectation, not a promise.

title: Two-trait crosses and independent assortment — video support
purpose: List valid gametes for two loci, use a Punnett square or product rule, and identify the assumption of independent assortment.
fallback: For AaBb × AaBb, the A locus gives a 3/4 dominant-phenotype probability and 1/4 recessive probability. The B locus gives the same. If the loci assort independently, the probability of both dominant phenotypes is 3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16. The other phenotype combinations are 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16, producing the familiar 9:3:3:1 expectation. This ratio is specific to the stated heterozygote cross and allele relationships. For a different cross, recompute. In AaBb × aaBb, probability of A_ is 1/2 and probability of B_ is 3/4, so both dominant phenotypes have probability 3/8. A memorized 9/16 would be wrong.

title: Sex-linked inheritance — video support
purpose: Use a typical XX/XY model to solve X-linked crosses and distinguish conditional from joint probabilities.
fallback: Consider XBXb × XBY. The four equally likely combinations are XBXB, XBXb, XBY and XbY. One of four children is expected to be affected. Among sons only, one of two is expected to be affected. The probability of “a son who is affected” is 1/4 among all children. The probability that “the next son is affected” is 1/2 conditional on being a son. The wording changes the denominator, not the biological cross. An affected father passes his X chromosome to daughters and his Y to sons in this model. Father-to-son transmission therefore is not expected for an X-linked allele through that direct chromosome path.

title: Multiple alleles and ABO blood groups — video support
purpose: Use the ABO model to distinguish population allele diversity from individual genotype and solve blood-group crosses.
fallback: Type A can be IAIA or IAi. Type B can be IBIB or IBi. Type AB is IAIB, and type O is ii in the standard model. The phenotypes A and B leave genotype uncertainty unless additional family information is available. An individual with type B and a type O parent must have inherited i from that parent. Therefore the type B individual's genotype is IBi. This is the same constraint reasoning used in a test cross. Use clear notation. IAIB represents two alleles of one gene, not four separate genes. In plain text, write IA and IB consistently and keep the allele pairs grouped.

title: Reading autosomal pedigrees — video support
purpose: Read pedigree symbols and generations, infer autosomal genotypes under a stated model, and preserve unresolved alternatives.
fallback: For an autosomal recessive model, affected individuals are aa. Two unaffected parents with an affected child must each contribute a. If both are unaffected, each is therefore Aa under the simple fully penetrant model. For an autosomal dominant model, unaffected individuals are dd. An affected parent with an unaffected child must be able to contribute d, so that affected parent is Dd rather than DD. The child's genotype constrains the parent's possible alleles. These deductions use the stated model, accurate relationships and complete expression. New mutations, reduced penetrance or other complexities can change the interpretation; do not add them silently to a simple problem.

title: Sex-linked pedigrees and testing a model — video support
purpose: Use chromosome transmission to evaluate X-linked models and distinguish consistency from proof in small pedigrees.
fallback: An affected father in an X-linked dominant model passes the affected X to every daughter. With an unaffected mother, sons receive the father's Y and the mother's unaffected X, so they are unaffected under that model. For X-linked recessive inheritance, an affected father with a homozygous unaffected mother has carrier daughters and unaffected sons. The same chromosome route produces a different expressed pattern because the heterozygote phenotype differs. More affected males can be a clue to an X-linked recessive model, but sex counts alone are not decisive. A small autosomal family can also show an uneven distribution by chance.

title: Polygenic traits and environmental influences — video support
purpose: Explain polygenic and environmental contributions, and distinguish genotype, gene expression and measured phenotype.
fallback: Nutrition, temperature and other conditions can influence a phenotype. Plants with similar genotypes may reach different heights under different light or nutrient conditions. The measured difference does not automatically establish a difference in DNA sequence. Gene expression describes which genetic information is used and how much product is made. Cells with the same inherited genome can have different functions because they express different sets of genes. Environmental or developmental signals can change expression. Some regulatory changes involve chemical modifications associated with DNA or chromatin. These are often discussed as epigenetic changes. Do not treat every such change as a mutation or assume it is always inherited through many generations.

title: Linked genes and recombinant offspring — video support
purpose: Identify linked allele arrangements, parental and recombinant combinations, and use a test cross to interpret gamete frequencies.
fallback: Cross a heterozygote with aabb. The tester contributes only ab, so the offspring's phenotype or genotype can reveal the heterozygote's gamete contribution. Under independent assortment, the four combinations are expected in equal proportions. If the heterozygote has AB/ab and the genes are linked, AB and ab gametes often occur more frequently than Ab and aB. The corresponding parental offspring classes are larger, and the recombinant classes smaller. Read the actual counts, not just the presence of four categories. Linked genes can produce all four combinations if crossing over occurs, but the proportions can differ from 1:1:1:1.

title: Recombination frequency and chromosome maps — video support
purpose: Calculate recombination frequency, construct simple maps and distinguish map distance from a universal physical base-pair distance.
fallback: Suppose A–B is 6 map units, B–C is 14 and A–C is 20 in a simple additive map. Since 6 + 14 = 20, B lies between A and C. Either A—6—B—14—C or its reversed orientation expresses the same relative order. Two distances alone may leave more than one order possible. Place the genes tentatively and ask what additional comparison would distinguish the alternatives. Do not invent a third distance merely to finish the drawing.
